slides.header: Upstairs feels like an oven? Your roof might be why.
August is when you feel it
slides.body: A poorly vented attic bakes all summer. Upstairs rooms won't cool down, and shingles cooked from below age years ahead of schedule.

slides.header: Your attic is supposed to breathe
slides.body: Cool air enters low through the soffit vents, warms in the attic, rises, and exits near the ridge. No fans required. Physics runs it around the clock.
Exhaust without intake just stalls. When we chase ventilation problems, blocked soffit vents (usually stuffed with insulation) are the culprit as often as missing exhaust.
A continuous vent along the ridge exhausts evenly, exactly where rising warm air wants to leave. No motors or bearings to die, and nearly invisible.

slides.header: One rule: don't mix exhaust types
slides.body: A ridge vent plus old box vents sounds like extra airflow, but it short-circuits the loop. When we install a ridge vent, retiring the old exhaust is part of the job.
